c.tagline: Botswana's understated capital, gateway to safari country.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are used for short in-town trips; for longer journeys or airport transfers, agree the fare with the driver before departing.

emergency.note: 998 reaches the fire brigade; these toll-free numbers work from any phone, including mobiles.

hood_landmark.Gaborone West (Grand Palm): Grand Palm Hotel Casino Convention Resort

avoid.reason: Avoid the Old Naledi township and walking anywhere in the city after dark.
Bag- and phone-snatching around the main bus rank and Main Mall; use taxis at night.

hood_desc: Gaborone's walkable government and business core around the pedestrian Main Mall, with banks, the stock exchange, and government offices. Suits business travelers and first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.

A leafy, established diplomatic and residential district near the National Museum, known for owner-run guesthouses and quiet tree-lined streets. Suits travelers wanting a homely, low-key base close to the center.

A hotel-and-retail cluster built around Airport Junction Mall on the A1 just north of the CBD, minutes from Sir Seretse Khama International Airport. Suits transit travelers, early departures, and business visitors needing airport proximity.

Home to the sprawling Grand Palm casino-and-convention resort with pools, restaurants, and nightlife on the western edge of the city. Suits conference delegates, families, and travelers wanting resort-style amenities.
A quieter southern district at the foot of Kgale Hill, close to Mokolodi Nature Reserve and hiking trails. Suits nature-minded travelers and those breaking a journey to or from safari lodges.

water.note: Officially treated and chlorinated, but water-quality audits and rural inconsistencies mean bottled water is the safer choice.

transit.pay: Fares on buses and combis are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in Botswana Pula; there is no rechargeable transit card. Fares are flat-rate by route, so keep small change on hand.
transit.hours: Buses and combis generally operate from around 6am to 8pm with sparse Sunday service; there is little to no service after dark, so taxis or ride-hailing apps are needed at night.
transit.note: A limited Botswana Railways passenger line passes through Gaborone toward Lobatse and Francistown, but most residents and visitors rely on combis, buses, and taxis for getting around.

bus: Local combi minibuses and intercity coaches from the main bus rank

tip.r: Tipping is not deeply ingrained but is appreciated; round up or add roughly 10% at sit-down restaurants, and tip safari guides, drivers, and porters directly in cash.

food.name: Seswaa
food.desc: Botswanas national dish: beef or goat boiled long in salted water then pounded to soft shreds, served with maize or sorghum porridge.

places.name: Iketsetseng Restaurant

places.name: Botswanacraft Restaurant
places.note: Traditional buffet in a craft-village setting, popular with visitors.

food.name: Bogobe jwa Lerotse
food.desc: Sorghum porridge, sometimes cooked with sweet lerotse melon; the everyday Setswana staple eaten with meat and relish.

places.name: Iketsetseng Restaurant
places.note: Serves proper sorghum bogobe rather than only maize pap.

food.desc: Wild leafy greens gathered after the rains, stewed with onion and tomato and eaten as relish beside porridge and meat.

food.name: Serobe

landmarks: Three Dikgosi Monument
A striking bronze tribute to three revered 19th-century Tswana chiefs, this monument anchors Gaborone's Main Mall and is the city's most photographed cultural landmark.
National Museum of Botswana
Botswana's premier museum showcases natural history, ethnography, and art, offering visitors an engaging introduction to the country's cultural and biological heritage.
Kgale Hill
Gaborone's iconic hillside backdrop rewards hikers with sweeping panoramic views over the city and the sparkling waters of Gaborone Dam below.
Botswana National Botanical Garden
A tranquil oasis of indigenous flora near the city center, this garden is beloved for its walking trails, birdlife, and striking desert-adapted plant collections.
Gaborone Dam
This vast reservoir framed by rocky hills is a favorite spot for scenic photography, birdwatching, and picnicking just outside the capital.
Mokolodi Nature Reserve
A wildlife sanctuary just south of the city where visitors can spot rhinos, giraffes, and zebras on game drives without leaving the Gaborone area.
Parliament Building of Botswana
The seat of Botswana's democratic government, this dignified building symbolizes the nation's stability and is a notable stop on any civic tour of Gaborone.
Botswana National Stadium
The country's largest sporting arena hosts major football matches and national celebrations, standing as a modern landmark of civic pride in Gaborone.
Main Mall
Gaborone's pedestrian heart blends open-air markets, shops, and government buildings, making it the liveliest place to soak up everyday city life.
Gaborone Game Reserve
A surprisingly accessible urban reserve where impala, zebra, and rhino roam close to downtown, offering an easy wildlife encounter within the capital itself.

train.note: Botswana Railways' overnight BR Express normally links Lobatse-Gaborone-Francistown with seats and sleepers, but the operator's website currently shows the passenger service as SUSPENDED - check before relying on it. No international passenger trains run through Gaborone.

bus.note: Intercape coaches to South Africa depart Gaborone; book online and bring your passport for the Ramatlabama/Tlokweng border. Shared minibus 'combis' also cross to Johannesburg and toward Zimbabwe (Bulawayo).

ferry.note: Botswana is landlocked - no ferries. The former Kazungula ferry to Zambia (far north) was replaced by the Kazungula Bridge in 2021.
